target_customer: Startups and small companies wanting bug bounty or managed pentesting programs
problem: Bug bounty platforms (HackerOne, Bugcrowd) served large enterprises at high cost; startups lacked security staff.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on bounties plus later paid managed plans and pentests
product_category: Bug bounty and penetration testing platform

founders.name: William Sulinski
founders.background_notes: Twin brother of James per TechCrunch; surname given in TechCrunch.

founders.name: James Sulinski
prior_employers: MoPub (director of engineering, acquired by Twitter 2013)
founders.background_notes: Early MoPub engineer handling security and infrastructure.

competitors.name: HackerOne
competitors.what: Bug bounty platform aimed mainly at large enterprises, six-figure pricing per founders

competitors.name: Bugcrowd
competitors.what: Bug bounty platform aimed mainly at larger organizations

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace and report triage software; the hard part was vetting researchers and filtering low-quality reports, not core technology.

defensibility.rationale: Researcher supply could create a weak two-sided network, but incumbents could add a startup tier and founders had no proprietary data or lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence found of incumbents copying or buying Federacy; sources do not say.

market_need_then: Founders' Launch HN (2018-08-02) said startups could not afford enterprise bounty platforms or hire security staff; TechCrunch reported over 120 sign-ups after launch.

brand_strength.rationale: Name suggests federation/community; no sourced evidence of brand strength or recall.

pivots.from: Free-to-set-up bug bounty marketplace taking a cut of bounties
pivots.to: Managed bug bounty and pentest plans with paid tiers (site later lists a $599/month plan)
pivots.why: Not stated by sources; inferred from site changes only, so treat as weak.

outcome_analysis: The YC directory marks Federacy Inactive, but no shutdown notice, post-mortem or acquisition was found, so the cause is not public. It launched with 120+ sign-ups in August 2018 and a thin market position between enterprise bounty platforms and cheap pentest shops; a later search turned up site pages still advertising paid plans. Not enough evidence to assign failure factors.
notes: Conflict: YC page says Inactive and one tracker says Active; federacy.com/bugbounties appears to advertise plans (search result, undated) while the home page fetch returned 404. Cause and date of any shutdown are not public. CB Insights snippet shows a ~$120K seed (2018-08) with YC; single aggregator so unverified, not recorded as a round. Founders' first names from YC page; surname from TechCrunch. Launch HN is a repost on a personal blog. Completeness pass: the 120K seed (2018-08-10) rests on CB Insights alone; TechCrunch covered the launch but gave no amount.
